records.condition: the sheet marks this as required by another instrument (its legend: ESPR / JTC-24), not by the Batteries Regulation
records.definition: The reference standard the DPP instance schema refers to
records.requirement_regulation: The reference standard the DPP instance schema refers to.

records.condition: the sheet marks this as required by another instrument (its legend: ESPR / JTC-24), not by the Batteries Regulation
records.definition: The current status of the DPP as a digital resource
records.requirement_regulation: The status of the DPP instance as digital resource. Example: "Active", "Archived"

records.condition: the sheet marks this as required by another instrument (its legend: ESPR / JTC-24), not by the Batteries Regulation
records.definition: The required level of information with regard to product item, batch or model
records.requirement_regulation: The level of granularity of the ProductID as per ESPR: model, batch or item In the Battery passport the value shall be 'Item' as each battery will have an individual battery passport.

records.text: Date-time of latest update of DPP
records.condition: the sheet marks this as required by another instrument (its legend: ESPR / JTC-24), not by the Batteries Regulation
records.definition: Date and time of the latest update of the battery passport
records.requirement_regulation: The date and time of the latest update to the DPP instance.
records.update_requirement: upon any update of the battery passport

records.text: Unique battery passport identifier / unique DPP identifier
records.definition: The unique identifier of a battery passport, equivalent to the unique DPP identifier in JTC-24 draft standards
records.requirement_regulation: The unique battery passport identifier / unique DPP identifier serves distinction and identification of archived versions and should resolve to one specific version of a battery passport. Note: The JTC-24 standards foresee an archiving function for DPPs after updates (exceptions to dynamic data may apply). Note: A new battery passport version after an update will obtain a new unique battery passport identifier / unique DPP identifier. The previous unique battery passport identifier / unique DPP identifier will be archived together with its previous battery passport version. The initial unique battery passport identifier / unique DPP identifier, likely to be stored in the EU DPP registry, therefore always resolves to the first version of a battery passport.
records.update_requirement: upon any update of the battery passport that includes archiving

records.text: Unique battery identifier / unique product identifier
records.definition: The unique identifier of the battery item, equivalent to the unique product identifier in JTC-24 draft standards
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include information identifying the battery. The battery passport must be accessible through the QR code […] which links to a persistent unique battery identifier. The battery identifier is a unique string of characters for the identification of batteries that also enables a link to the battery passport. The battery identifier must comply with ISO/IEC 15459 1:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 2:2015, ISO/IEC 15459 3:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 4:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 5:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 6:2014, or their equivalent. It shall be based on a URI/URL structure. Note: According to JTC-24 prEN_18219 (4.) describes the unique product identifier (here: unique battery identifier shall follow the following principles: (4.1) globally uniqueness, (4.2) persistence, (4.3) syntax, (4.4) semantic, (4.5) Interoperability and (4.6) Openness. The economic operator placing the battery on the market must attribute the battery identifier to it. Note: The unique battery identifier / unique product identifier must also be provided on the battery label. Where the size or nature of the battery does not allow it, the required information must be provided on the packaging or in a document accompanying the battery.

records.definition: The unique identifier of the battery model.
records.requirement_regulation: The battery model identifier is a shared property of batteries that belong to the same battery model, which is a version of a battery all units of which share the same technical characteristics relevant for the requirements of the Battery Regulation on sustainability, safety, labelling,marking and information. Note: The model identifier is a unique string of characters and required in the Draft for the CF declaration IA.
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: Serial number of the battery including information on the battery batch
records.requirement_regulation: Note: The following requirements of the battery regulation, not directly addressing the battery passport, should be considered: Manufacturers shall ensure that batteries which they place on the market bear a model identification and batch or serial number, or product number or another element allowing their identification. Where the size or nature of the battery does not allow it, the required information shall be provided on the packaging or in a document accompanying the battery. The Declaration of Conformity requires the following information (among other information): "Battery model (product, category, and batch or serial number):"

records.condition: the sheet marks this as required by another instrument (its legend: ESPR / JTC-24), not by the Batteries Regulation
records.definition: The unique identifier of the economic operator
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include an operator identifier. The operator identifier is a unique string of characters for the identification of actors involved in the value chain of products (see ESPR, Article 2(31)). It corresponds to the economic operator responsible for creating or updating the battery passport. Where a unique operator identifier is not yet available, “the economic operator that creates or updates the digital product passport shall request a unique operator identifier on behalf of the relevant actor.” (see ESPR, Article 12(2)). The unique operator identifier must, where relevant for the products concerned, comply with ISO/IEC 15459 1:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 2:2015, ISO/IEC 15459 3:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 4:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 5:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 6:2014, or their equivalent until referenced harmonised standards are listed in the Official Journal of European Union (OJEU). (see also ESPR Annex III)
records.legal_reference: ESPR Art. 2 (31), 12 (2); Annex XIII (1a) Annex VI Part A; Art. 3(66); Art. 77 (3) JTC-24 prEN_18219 (4.1.1.1) (draft)
legal_references: Annex XIII (1a) Annex VI Part A
records.access_as_written: Notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission

records.definition: The unique identifier of the manufacturer of the battery.
records.requirement_regulation: The unique manufacturer identifier must, where relevant for the products concerned, comply with ISO/IEC 15459 1:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 2:2015, ISO/IEC 15459 3:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 4:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 5:2014, ISO/IEC 15459 6:2014, or equivalent European or international standards until referenced harmonised standards are listed in the OJEU (see also ESPR Annex III).
records.legal_reference: Annex VI Part A (1); Art. 38(7); ESPR Art. 2(32); ESPR Art. 12(1); ESPR Annex III
records.access_as_written: Notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission

records.condition: the sheet marks this as required by another instrument (its legend: ESPR / JTC-24), not by the Batteries Regulation
records.definition: The unique identifier of a facility
records.requirement_regulation: A unique facility identifier is a unique string of characters for the identification of locations or buildings involved in a product’s value chain or used by actors involved in a product’s value chain. (JTC-24 prEN_18219 (3.20)) The unique facility identifiers shall, where relevant for the products concerned, comply with standards ISO/IEC 15459-1:2014, ISO/IEC 15459-2:2015, ISO/IEC 15459-3:2014, ISO/IEC 15459-4:2014, ISO/IEC 15459-5:2014 and ISO/IEC 15459-6:2014. (ESPR Annex III)
records.legal_reference: JTC-24 prEN_18219 (3.20) (draft); JTC-24 prEN_18219 (draft); ESPR Annex III
records.access_as_written: Notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission

records.definition: Information related to the economic operator
Information related to the manufacturer of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include information identifying the manufacturer. The manufacturer information must also be provided on the battery label. Where it is not possible to indicate the required information on the battery, it must be provided on the packaging or in a document accompanying the battery. The manufacturer information must include: - name; - registered trade name or registered trademark; - postal address, indicating a single contact point; - web address, if available; and - e-mail address, if available. The contact details must be indicated in a language or languages which can be easily understood by end-users and market surveillance authorities.
records.legal_reference: Annex VI Part A (1); Art. 3, 1(33); Art. 38(7)

records.definition: The place of manufacture of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the manufacturing place (geographical location of a battery manufacturing plant). It must be indicated as town, region and country/jurisdiction. The manufacturing place must also be provided on the battery label.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1a); Annex VI, Part A(3); Labelling IA (draft)

records.definition: The date of manufacture of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the date of manufacture (month and year). The manufacturing date must also be provided on the battery label. The manufacturing date must consist of the month and year of the date of manufacture.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1a); Annex VI Part A (4); Annex VII Part B (1); Labelling IA (draft)

records.text: Date of putting the battery into service
records.definition: The date of first use, for its intended purpose, in the European Union, of a battery, without having been previously placed on the market
records.requirement_regulation: Where appropriate, the battery passport must include information on the date of putting the battery into service.

records.definition: Commercial warranty period for the battery
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include information about the period for which the commercial warranty applies.

records.definition: Description of the scope of application of a battery in terms of its use according to the battery regulation
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the battery category. The battery category must be provided on the battery label. The battery must be categorised by its intended use in: - LMT battery; - electric vehicle battery; or - industrial battery (stationary battery energy storage system/other industrial batteries).
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1a); Annex VI Part A (2)

records.definition: The mass of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the battery weight. Note: In all other instances we use the term mass instead of weight, which is used in the regulation: Regulatory requirements define the unit as kg or g per regulation and the physically correct term is then mass. The battery mass must also be provided on the battery label.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1a); Annex VI Part A (5); Labelling IA (draft)

records.definition: Current status of the battery item in its life cycle
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include information on the status of the battery. The status of the battery must be defined as ‘original’, ‘repurposed’, ‘re-used’, ‘remanufactured’ or ‘waste’. A new battery passport must be issued when a battery was subject to remanufacturing, repurpose or one of the treatment operations preparing for re-use and preparing for repurpose and is placed on the market again.
records.update_requirement: upon placement on market and battery status change

records.category: Symbols, labels and documentation of conformity
records.definition: Symbol indicating the necessity of separate collection
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include the symbol for separate collection. All batteries must be marked on the label with the symbol for separate collection from 18 August 2025. The separate collection symbol must cover at least 3 % of the area of the largest side of the battery with a maximum size of (5 × 5) cm2. For Cylindrical battery cells: The symbol must cover at least 1,5 % of the surface area of the battery and with a maximum size of (5 × 5) cm2. Where the symbol would be smaller than (0,47 × 0,47) cm2, the battery does not need to be marked with it. Instead, the symbol measuring at least (1 × 1) cm2 must be printed on the packaging.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1s); Art. 13(4); Annex VI Part B

records.category: Symbols, labels and documentation of conformity
records.definition: Representation of the chemical symbol “Cd” for cadmium and “Pb” for lead contained in the battery
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include information regarding the prevention and management of waste batteries including the meaning of the labels and symbols on batteries or printed on their packaging or in the documents accompanying batteries. Batteries containing more than 0,002 % cadmium or more than 0,004 % lead, must be marked with the chemical symbol for the metal concerned: Cd or Pb. The symbols for cadmium and lead must also be provided on the battery label. The relevant chemical symbol indicating the heavy metal content must be printed beneath the separate collection symbol and must cover an area of at least one-quarter the size of that symbol.

records.category: Symbols, labels and documentation of conformity
records.definition: Label indicating the carbon footprint and carbon footprint performance class
records.requirement_regulation: EV batteries, rechargeable industrial batteries > 2 kWh and LMT batteries shall bear a conspicuous, clearly legible and indelible label indicating the carbon footprint and declaring the carbon footprint performance class to which the relevant battery model per manufacturing plant corresponds. The format of the label is described in the Labelling IA and shall include: Reference to the relevant delegated act establishing the carbon footprint performance classes according to Article 7(2), fourth subparagraph, point (a) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the relevant battery category; Declaration of the carbon footprint performance class based on the relevant delegated act establishing the carbon footprint performance classes; Declared life-cycle carbon footprint expressed in a resolution of two significant figures in accordance with the methodology set out in the relevant delegated acts; The functional unit in accordance with the methodology set out in the relevant delegated acts adopted by the Commission.
records.legal_reference: Article 7(2) via Annex XIII (1c); Labelling IA (draft) Annex V
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.category: Symbols, labels and documentation of conformity
records.definition: Specification of the usable extinguishing agent
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the usable extinguishing agent or if relevant, the fire class of that agent determined in accordance with standard EN 2:2005 The usable extinguishing agent must also be provided on the battery label.
records.legal_reference: Annex VI Part A (9); Labelling IA (draft)

records.category: Symbols, labels and documentation of conformity
records.definition: Brief and easily understandable explanatory sentence conveying the meaning of symbols and labels used
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include information regarding the prevention and management of waste batteries including the meaning of the labels and symbols on batteries or printed on their packaging or in the documents accompanying batteries. The information must be communicated in (a) language(s) easily understood by end-users. All labels and symbols used in the battery label must be accompanied by a brief and easily understandable explanatory sentence.

records.category: Symbols, labels and documentation of conformity
records.definition: The document that declares compliance with requirements for placement on EU market
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the EU declaration of conformity. The regulation specifies the following requirements regarding the EU declaration of conformity (see BattReg Annex XIII (1r) and BattReg Article 18 (2)): - The EU declaration of conformity has the model structure set out in Annex IX. - The EU declaration of conformity must contain the elements specified in the relevant modules set out in Annex VIII. - The EU declaration of conformity must be kept up to date. - It is translated into the language or languages required by the Member State in which the battery is placed or made available on the market or put into service. - It must be drawn up in electronic format and, where requested, it must be provided in paper format.
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.text: Results of test reports proving compliance
records.category: Symbols, labels and documentation of conformity
records.definition: Test report results proving compliance with the requirements stated in the battery regulation
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the test report results that can prove the compliance with the requirements stated in the battery regulation.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (3); Annex VIII Part A 2(h)
records.access_as_written: Notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.text: Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit
records.definition: The battery carbon footprint must be included as declared in terms of kg of carbon dioxide equivalent per one kWh of the total energy provided by the battery over its expected service life.
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must contain carbon footprint per functional unit of the battery as declared in the battery carbon footprint declaration in accordance with the entry into force of the implementing acts on the format of declaration.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1c) → Art. 7; EV CF DA (draft); CF declaration IA (draft)
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.text: Contribution of raw material acquisition and pre-processing lifecycle stage
records.definition: Contribution of raw material acquisition and pre-processing lifecycle stage to the battery carbon footprint
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the contribution of the lifecycle stage “Raw material acquisition and pre-processing” in the battery carbon footprint. The system boundaries and reporting requirements are specified in the delegated acts for the carbon footprint methodology outlined in "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" The same mandatory requirements as for "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" are required for this data point.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1c) → Art. 7; Annex II (4); EV CF DA (draft); CF declaration IA (draft)
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.text: Contribution of main product production lifecycle stage
records.definition: Contribution of the main product production lifecycle stage to the battery carbon footprint
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the contribution of the lifecycle stage “Main product production” in the battery carbon footprint. The system boundaries and reporting requirements are specified in the delegated acts for the carbon footprint methodology outlined in "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" The same mandatory requirements as for "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" are required for this data point.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1c) → Art. 7; Annex II (4); EV CF DA (draft); CF declaration IA (draft)
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: Contribution of the distribution lifecycle stage to the battery's carbon footprint
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the contribution of the lifecycle stage “Distribution” in the battery carbon footprint. The system boundaries and reporting requirements are specified in the delegated acts for the carbon footprint methodology outlined in "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" The same mandatory requirements as for "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" are required for this data point.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII 1(c) → Art. 7; Annex II (4); EV CF DA (draft); CF declaration IA (draft)
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.text: Contribution of end of life and recycling lifecycle stage
records.definition: Contribution of the end of life and recycling lifecycle stage to the battery's carbon footprint
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include the contribution of the lifecycle stage “End of life and Recycling” in the battery carbon footprint. The system boundaries and reporting requirements are specified in the delegated acts for the carbon footprint methodology outlined in "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" The same mandatory requirements as for "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit" are required for this data point.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1c) → Art. 7; Annex II (4); EV CF DA (draft); CF declaration IA (draft)
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: Depending on the distribution of the values in the carbon footprint declarations of batteries placed on the market, a meaningful number of classes of performance shall be identified, with category A being the best class with the lowest carbon footprint life cycle impact, to enable market differentiation
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include the carbon footprint performance class in accordance with the entry into force of the delegated and implementing acts on the carbon footprint performance classes per Article 7 of the Battery Regulation. The carbon footprint performance class shall be indicated on the carbon footprint label.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1c); Art. 7(2); Labelling IA (draft) Annex V
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.text: Web link to public carbon footprint study
records.definition: The public version of the carbon footprint study
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include a web link to the carbon footprint study accompanying the battery carbon footprint declaration. The information and reporting requirements are specified in the corresponding delegated acts as outlined in 6.3.2 "Battery carbon footprint per Functional Unit".
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1c); Art. 7 1(g); EV CF DA (draft)
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: Battery carbon footprint as absolute number
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: The report on the supply chain due diligence policy, risk management plan, and summary of third-party verification.
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include the “information on responsible sourcing as indicated in the report on its due diligence policy referred to in BattReg Article 52(3)”. The due diligence report must be accessible free of charge to the public via the battery passport and also on the internet. The report and hence also the information in the battery passport must provide data and information on four aspects: - Supply chain due diligence policy: steps taken by the economic operator to comply with the requirements of Article 49. - Risk management plan: steps taken by the economic operator to comply with the requirements of Article 50, including findings of significant adverse impacts. - Summary report of the third-party verification carried out (Article 51). - An elaboration on access to information, public participation in decision-making and access to justice.

records.text: Third party assurances of recognised schemes
records.definition: Information on supply chain scheme assurances granted by third-party actors
Information on relevant supply chain indices
The electrochemical composition reflecting active materials in cathode and anode, and - voluntarily - electrolyte
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must contain information on the battery chemistry of the battery. The battery chemistry must also be provided on the battery label Base on the labelling IA (currently available as draft), the following terms shall be used: Lead acid: “Pb” Nickel cadmium: “Ni-Cd” Nickel metal hydride: “Ni-MH” Lithium ion NMC: “Li-ion NMC” Lithium ion LFP: “Li-ion LFP” Lithium ion LMO: “Li-ion LMO” Lithium ion LCO: “Li-ion LCO” Lithium ion NCA: “Li-ion NCA” Lithium metal: “Li-metal” Sodium-ion: “Na-ion” For secondary (rechargeable) batteries whose electrochemical composition does not correspond to any of the categories listed above, it shall be indicated based on the molecular formula of the cathode and/or anode.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1b); Annex VI Part A (7); Labelling IA (draft)

records.definition: Critical raw materials present in a concentration of more than 0,1%, weight by weight
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must contain information on the critical raw materials present in the battery. Critical raw materials are listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2024/1252. The information on the critical raw materials must also be provided on the battery label. Per Annex VI, Part A(10), critical raw materials must be reported if present in the battery in a concentration of more than 0,1 % weight by weight.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1b); Annex VI Part A (10); Labelling IA (draft)

records.text: Materials used in cathode, anode and electrolyte
records.definition: Detailed composition of cathode, anode and electrolyte
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must contain information on the detailed composition of the battery. Information on the detailed composition must include materials used in the cathode, anode and electrolyte.
records.access_as_written: persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission

records.definition: Substances of very high concern in the meaning of Article 3 (1) (69) which are present in the battery, other than mercury, cadmium and lead, with a concentration equal or above 0,1%, weight on weight.’
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must contain information on substances of very high concern other than mercury, cadmium, or lead contained in the battery. substances of very high concern in the meaning of Article 3 (1) (69) which are present in the battery, other than mercury, cadmium and lead, with a concentration equal or above 0,1%, weight on weight. ‘substance of very high concern’ means any substance which fulfils the criteria laid down in Article 57 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 [REACH] and is identified in accordance with Article 59(1) of that Regulation, or any substance which fulfils the criteria laid down in Article 57 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 [REACH] and listed in Annex VI of Regulation (EC) 1272/2008 [CLP Regulation].’ Substances of very high concern and those for which there is a restriction in BattReg Annex I [mercury, cadmium, lead] are required to be named in accordance with their nomenclature in Regulation (EC) 1272/2008 ("CLP Regulation"). The information on hazardous substances must also be provided on the battery label. BattReg Article 74(3) states that the location of the hazardous substances in the battery must be identified. This requirement needs to be provided upon request even though it is not specifically for the battery passport and can be integrated.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1b); Annex VI Part A (8); Labelling IA (draft), Environmental Omnibus: Draft: 2025/0397 (COD), Art. 1 (4)
legal_references: Labelling IA (draft), Environmental Omnibus: Draft: 2025/0397 (COD), Art. 1 (4)

records.text: Impact of substances on environment, human health, safety, persons
records.definition: Elaboration on the impact of substances contained in the battery on the environment, human health and the safety of persons
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must contain information on the impact of substances, in particular hazardous substances, present in the battery. Hereby the impact on the environment and on human health or the safety of persons is considered and includes the impact due to inappropriate discarding of waste batteries, such as littering or discarding as unsorted municipal waste.

records.text: Dismantling information: Manuals for the removal and the disassembly of the battery pack
records.definition: Manual(s) containing information on the removal and disassembly of the battery pack
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include dismantling information. The dismantling information must include: - exploded diagrams of the battery system/pack showing the location of battery cells; - disassembly sequences; - type and number of fastening techniques to be unlocked; - tools required for disassembly; - warnings if risk of damaging parts exist; and - amount of cells used and layout.
records.access_as_written: persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission

records.definition: The part numbers of components of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include part numbers for components.
records.access_as_written: persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission

records.text: Information on sources of spare parts
records.definition: Information on how to contact sources of spare parts
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include contact details of sources for spare parts (replacement spares).
records.access_as_written: persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission

records.definition: Safety measures to be taken during battery handling, including the dismantling
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include safety measures.
records.access_as_written: persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission

records.definition: The share of nickel recycled from pre-consumer waste in the active materials of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include recycled content information. The content information must include the percentage share of nickel that is present in active materials and that has been recovered from battery manufacturing waste, for each battery model per year and per manufacturing plant. Pre-consumer waste or “battery manufacturing waste” is “the materials or objects rejected during the battery manufacturing process, which cannot be re-used as an integral part in the same process and need to be recycled”
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: The share of cobalt recycled from pre-consumer waste in the active materials of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include recycled content information. The content information must include the percentage share of cobalt that is present in active materials and that has been recovered from battery manufacturing waste, for each battery model per year and per manufacturing plant. Pre-consumer waste or “battery manufacturing waste” is “the materials or objects rejected during the battery manufacturing process, which cannot be re-used as an integral part in the same process and need to be recycled”
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: The share of lithium recycled from pre-consumer waste in the active materials of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include recycled content information. The content information must include the percentage share of lithium that is present in active materials and that has been recovered from battery manufacturing waste, for each battery model per year and per manufacturing plant. Pre-consumer waste or “battery manufacturing waste” is “the materials or objects rejected during the battery manufacturing process, which cannot be re-used as an integral part in the same process and need to be recycled”
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: The share of nickel recycled from post-consumer waste in the active materials of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include recycled content information. The content information must include the percentage share of nickel that is present in active materials and that has been recovered from post-consumer waste, for each battery model per year and per manufacturing plant.
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: The share of cobalt recycled from post-consumer waste in the active materials of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include recycled content information. The content information must include the percentage share of cobalt that is present in active materials and that has been recovered from post-consumer waste, for each battery model per year and per manufacturing plant.
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: The share of lithium recycled from post-consumer waste in the active materials of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include recycled content information. The content information must include the percentage share of lithium that is present in active materials and that has been recovered from post-consumer waste, for each battery model per year and per manufacturing plant.
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: The share of recycled lead in the active materials of the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include recycled content information. The content information must include the percentage share of lead that is present in the active materials of the battery and that has been recovered from waste, for each battery model per year and per manufacturing plant. The regulation does not distinguish between pre- and post-consumer waste for the lead share.
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.definition: Share of renewable content in the battery
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include information about the share of renewable content.
records.granularity: Battery model per calendar year and per manufacturing site, i.e. batch level

records.text: Information on the role of end-users in contributing to waste prevention
records.sub_category: Information on role of end-users in waste prevention and information on battery collection, preparation for second life and on treatment at end of life
records.definition: Information on how end-users can contribute to waste prevention
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include information on the role of end-users in contributing to waste prevention. The information must include good practices and recommendations concerning the use of batteries aimed at extending their use phase and the possibilities of re-use, preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing and remanufacturing.

records.text: Information on the role of end-users in contributing to the separate collection of waste batteries
records.sub_category: Information on role of end-users in waste prevention and information on battery collection, preparation for second life and on treatment at end of life
records.definition: Information on how end-users can contribute to the separate collection of waste batteries
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include information on the role of end-users in contributing to the separate collection of waste batteries. End-users are obliged to discard waste batteries separately from other waste streams, including from mixed municipal waste and in designated separate collection points set up by, or in accordance with the specific arrangements concluded with, the producer or a producer responsibility organisation.

records.text: Information on battery collection, preparation for second life and on treatment at end of life
records.sub_category: Information on role of end-users in waste prevention and information on battery collection, preparation for second life and on treatment at end of life
records.definition: Information on the collection of waste batteries, their preparation for second life and definitive treatment at end of life
records.requirement_regulation: A battery passport must include information on the separate collection, take-back and collection points, preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing and treatment available for waste batteries.

records.definition: The total number of ampere-hours that can be withdrawn from a fully charged battery under reference conditions
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include information about the rated capacity. The rated capacity of LMT batteries shall be determined according to reliable, accurate and reproducible methods which take into account the generally recognised state-of-the-art methods, and the results of which are deemed to be of low uncertainty, including methods set out in standards for which references have been published for those purposes in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJEU). Note: (For LMT batteries) the rated capacity is included in the required information for the battery label.
records.legal_reference: Annex IV Part A (1); Annex XIII (1g); Labelling IA (draft) Annex II Part A (VI) and Part C (C, 1)
legal_references: Labelling IA (draft) Annex II Part A (VI) and Part C (C, 1)

records.text: Initial internal resistance of battery cell and pack (module recommended)
records.definition: "Quotient of change of voltage of a battery by the corresponding change in discharge current under specified conditions” (IEV 482 03 36)
records.requirement_regulation: BattReg Annex IV (5) states that ‘Internal resistance’ means the opposition to the flow of current within a cell or a battery under reference conditions, that is, the sum of electronic resistance and ionic resistance to the contribution to total effective resistance including inductive/capacitive properties. This definition differs from the definition according to the IEC Electropedia stated above. The battery passport must include information about the internal resistance. The battery passport must include information about the internal resistance on both battery cell and pack level.
records.legal_reference: Annex XIII (1o); Art. 10: Annex IV Part A (3) (+definition of internal resistance)
legal_references: Art. 10: Annex IV Part A (3) (+definition of internal resistance)

records.text: Internal resistance increase of pack (cell and module recommended)
records.definition: The increase over time and upon usage of internal resistance
records.requirement_regulation: The battery passport must include information about the internal resistance increase. The internal resistance increase must be updated upon change of the battery status, which is associated with a new placement on market and described in 6.1.3.7 "battery status".
